subject: Count number of parameters from model in RStan

messages.author: 49e107cb0f8a3d27
messages.subject: Count number of parameters from model in RStan
parts: Say I'm using a model with both parameters and transformed parameters. How do I find the total number of parameters in each block separately in RStan? Using the model_pars or even things like the inits attribute, it couples the two sets of parameters so you can't distinguish the two.

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: Count number of parameters from model in RStan
parts:
On Sunday, February 28, 2016 at 2:16:59 PM UTC-5, Dustin Tran wrote:
Say I'm using a model with both parameters and transformed parameters. How do I find the total number of parameters in each block separately in RStan? Using the model_pars or even things like the inits attribute, it couples the two sets of parameters so you can't distinguish the two.

I don't think there is anything like that in RStan. Here is a function that returns the things in the parameters block.

get_stan_params <- function(object) {
  stopifnot(is(object, "stanfit"))
  params <- grep("context__.vals_r", fixed = TRUE, value = TRUE,
                 x = strsplit(get_cppcode(get_stanmodel(object)), "\n")[[1]])
  params <- sapply(strsplit(params, "\""), FUN = function(x) x[[2]])
  params <- intersect(params, object@model_pars)
  return(params)
}

Ben

messages.author: 49e107cb0f8a3d27
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Count number of parameters from model in RStan
parts:
Cool, this is fine. So to get the number of pars, I would do something like

model <- stan(file, data = data, iter = 1, chains = 1)
pars <- get_stan_params(model)
length(unlist(attributes(model)$inits[[1]][pars]))

dustin

messages.author: 49e107cb0f8a3d27
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Count number of parameters from model in RStan
parts: Awesome. In case this is useful when someone finds this thread in the future, I use the following code to count the number of local parameters—these are parameters that are not in the transformed block and are not hyperparameters given by another stan file.

get_stan_params <- function(object) {
  stopifnot(is(object, "stanfit"))
  params <- grep("context__.vals_r", fixed = TRUE, value = TRUE,
                 x = strsplit(get_cppcode(get_stanmodel(object)), "\n")[[1]])
  params <- sapply(strsplit(params, "\""), FUN = function(x) x[[2]])
  params <- intersect(params, object@model_pars)
  return(params)
}

count_params <- function(object, params) {
  stopifnot(is(object, "stanfit") || is(object, "stanmodel"))
  return(sum(sapply(object@par_dims[params], prod)))
}

full_model <- suppressMessages(stan(file, data = data, iter = 1, chains = 1))
local_model <- stan_model(local_file)
g_alpha <- vb(local_model, data=c(data,phi), iter=1)

pars_local <- get_stan_params(g_alpha)
pars_full <- get_stan_params(full_model)
pars <- sapply(pars_local, function(x) if (x %in% pars_full) return(x))
count_params(g_alpha, pars)

Dustin

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Count number of parameters from model in RStan
parts:
These should be retrievable through the class that's
generated for the Stan program. See the constrained_param_names()
and unconstrained_param_names() methods, which have boolean flags
indicating whether or not to include the transformed parameters
and generated quantities. It's not straightforward, because to literally
count them you'd have to run it three times and count the size of output
each time.

- Bob
